written: Sun Oct 11 2026, before the first workflow run of the day-one test; no measured number existed when this file was committed

sources.thresholds: docs/PLAN.md, section 'The day-one test' (the skeptic's numbers, docs/skeptic.md 'Evidence that one day can collect')

rule_for_changes: No threshold in this file is changed, loosened or added after a result exists. If one looks unfair, the result is reported against it as written and the objection goes under problems in docs/dayone-results.md.

kernels.k01_sum_fwd: s += a[i], i up, int64 accumulator over int32 elements
kernels.k02_add_fwd: c[i] = a[i] + b[i], i up, bound a.size()
kernels.k03_stencil: c[i] = a[i-1] + a[i] + a[i+1], i from 1 to size-2

design_fixed_before_any_run.element_type: int32_t in std::vector, accessed through operator[]; each kernel is a noinline function kern_<id> with external linkage

size_classes.rule: working set counts every array of the kernel; L1 = half of L1d, L2 = half of L2, RAM = four times the last-level cache capped at 256 MiB; cache sizes read from /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cache on the runner

builds.novec: the NONE flags plus -fno-vectorize (timing positive control)
builds.aa: the NONE binary copied to a second path; the two must have equal sha256

timing.order: ABBA repeated (A B B A A B B A ...), one process per repetition
timing.clock: clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) inside the binary around the timed loop; process start, input fill and one warm-up call are excluded
timing.inner_iterations: calibrated once per cell on the NONE build to about 75 ms per process, then reused unchanged for every build of that cell
timing.sample: nanoseconds per kernel call (or per program iteration) for one process
timing.ratio: median(B) / median(A), where A is NONE
timing.interval: percentile bootstrap, 10000 resamples of each side independently, seed 20261011, 95 %

programs.json_parse: nlohmann/json release v3.11.3 (single header json.hpp from the release assets) parsing twitter.json from the simdjson repository at tag v3.10.1; the file's sha256 is recorded by the run
programs.second_program: the first of fmt 11.0.2 then pugixml 1.14 that builds against libc++-18 with NONE and FAST (SPEC section 3 order, yaml-cpp skipped because it needs a CMake build; tinyxml2 not reached unless both fail)

design_fixed_before_any_run.traps: number of ud2 instructions plus calls to __libcpp_verbose_abort in the kern_<id> function (kernels) or in the whole binary (programs), from objdump -d

criteria.plan_text: One Actions run times two byte-identical NONE binaries, 20 alternating reps each. If the bootstrap 95% CI half-width is 0.3% or less, the whole-program column can test 0.30%. If it is 1% or more, that column stays a sanity check.
criteria.measured_value: the largest half_width_pct over all aa_pairs
criteria.met_if: every A/A pair is byte-identical (equal sha256) and has 20 valid reps per side, so the floor is measured

branch.between: 0.3 < largest half-width < 1.0: the plan names no branch; the whole-program column stays a sanity check that prints its floor

criteria.note: C1 is met when the floor is measured; the branch decides what the whole-program column may claim, not GO

criteria.plan_text: If FAST costs 1.5x or more on reverse and strided loops in cache and under 2% on forward loops, the map has a headline a stranger can check.
met_if_all: for k04_rev and k05_stride2 at L1 and L2: ci95_lo of ratio FAST/NONE >= 1.5
for k01_sum_fwd, k02_add_fwd and k03_stencil at L1 and L2: ci95_hi of ratio FAST/NONE < 1.02
in every one of those cells the NONE and FAST output checksums are equal

criteria.plan_text: Build nlohmann/json and one more program against libc++-18-dev with FAST and NONE and count the traps.
met_if_all: json_parse builds with NONE and FAST, runs, and its NONE and FAST output checksums are equal
a second program builds with NONE and FAST, runs, and its NONE and FAST output checksums are equal
the trap count is recorded for both builds of both programs

informational_checks_not_in_go.text: From the compiler's own remarks: k01, k02, k03 vectorized in NONE and FAST; k04 and k05 vectorized in NONE and not vectorized in FAST (the skeptic's Compiler Explorer reading, re-checked on int32 and the runner's clang-18)
Every FAST kernel binary has more traps in kern_<id> than its NONE twin, or the FAST build is shown by the binary's printed _LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE value

go_rule: GO if C1_aa_floor, C2_loop_shape and C3_toolchain are all met. NO-GO otherwise; a NO-GO on C2 means the honest verdict is 'holds everywhere we looked' (docs/PLAN.md).

verdict_rule_spec_section_1.kernel_aa_floor_pct: the largest half_width_pct over the kernel A/A pairs (k02_add_fwd at L1, L2, RAM)
verdict_rule_spec_section_1.lost_vectorization: a kernel vectorized in NONE and not vectorized in FAST, from the remarks
verdict_rule_spec_section_1.not_on_axis: a kernel not vectorized in NONE is reported and not used for N or for the forward limit
verdict_rule_spec_section_1.positive_control_seen: OPERATIONALIZED HERE (SPEC says 'seen' without a number): at least one in-cache cell of a kernel vectorized in NONE has a NONE-NOVEC/NONE ratio with ci95_lo > 1 + kernel_aa_floor_pct/100
order: INCONCLUSIVE if an A/A pair is not byte-identical, or kernel_aa_floor_pct >= forward_limit_pct, or the positive control is not seen, or a checksum differs between builds of an in-cache cell

MAP if every forward kernel vectorized in both builds has, at L1 and L2, ci95_hi < 1 + forward_limit_pct/100, AND every lost-vectorization kernel has, at L1 and L2, ci95_lo >= reverse_min_ratio, AND at least one kernel lost vectorization
HOLDS_EVERYWHERE if no in-cache cell on the vectorization axis has ci95_lo >= 1 + forward_limit_pct/100 (X = the largest ratio upper bound, as a percent)
INCONCLUSIVE otherwise (a mixed picture that fits neither line)
verdict_rule_spec_section_1.N: median ratio over the lost-vectorization kernels at L1 and L2, with min and max; RAM cells reported but not in N
